# Inverse Query Tradeoffs

This repository studies binary discrimination between two known first columns
of an unknown unitary whose remaining columns are arbitrary. It counts total
forward and inverse oracle calls separately. The connected scientific account
is organized by topic under science/.

## Canonical entrypoints

- README.md: scientific question, principal results, specialist and learning
  routes, reproduction command, consequential scope, purpose and contact.
- science/model.md: authoritative promise, quantifiers, query and control
  contract, trace-distance convention, U1/L1/U2/C1/C2 and proof dependencies.
- science/dicke_calibration.md: exact calibration, hidden-basis Dicke probe,
  second and fourth moments, finite-angle success and rounded budgets;
  also the restricted fixed-occupation parallel variance bound.
- science/implementations.md: wide reversible-routing and streaming circuits,
  coherent reservoir, gate and memory accounting, known-gate precision,
  inverse-only phase-memory construction and synthesized-inverse resources.
- science/mixed_query_lower_bound.md: mixed-query Haar hard ensemble,
  projected path records, exact number identity, inverse-event hybrids,
  adaptive forward progress, projection leakage and finite converse constants.
- science/haar_simulation.md: Lemma HS.1 and its source-to-lemma derivation
  for a common environment, coherent skips, query directions and retained
  classical histories, with the explicit mixed-query dimension error.
- science/resource_tradeoffs.md: meaning of the resource boundary, constant
  factor sufficiency, expensive-inverse allocation, readable permutation
  calibration and the physical meaning of the two implementations.
- science/forward_only.md: all-dimension native-forward upper bound, QURA
  interface and global phase, calibration-only synthesis, integer allocation,
  ancillas, compilation costs and comparison with the known-state benchmark.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: imported ingredients, precise source interfaces,
  nearby resource models, attribution and scope of the literature comparison.
- references/references.bib: bibliographic identities and source editions.
- verification/README.md: reproducible finite checks, expected output and
  their scientific limits.
- verification/run_all.py: reproduction runner for the finite constructive
  checks; verification/requirements.txt records the required packages.

## Learning entrypoints

- learning/MILESTONES.md: canonical project-defined map, exactly M01–M30,
  with 10 background/preliminaries and 20 narrative/innovation milestones.
  Each milestone
  records a central question, an understanding target, earlier dependencies,
  a conceptual connection and scientific source pointers.
- learning/CHILDS_BRIDGE.md: the single selected educational anchor, Andrew
  M. Childs's Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, 17 April 2025. It provides
  targeted section references, notation and access translations, and original
  connections from the source to this project's mechanisms and proof.

## Reader routes

- To understand the scientific story: read science/model.md, then
  science/dicke_calibration.md and science/mixed_query_lower_bound.md; join
  their conclusions in science/resource_tradeoffs.md. Use
  science/implementations.md for the physical realization and
  science/forward_only.md for the dimension-dependent consequence.
- For self-directed study: follow learning/MILESTONES.md alongside
  learning/CHILDS_BRIDGE.md. The map is independent of a particular reader's
  prior knowledge. The bridge selects lookups within one source and explains
  the project-specific connections; it does not require reading the whole
  textbook before entering the science.
- To inspect an exact theorem: begin with science/model.md and follow its
  canonical proof link. Trace a lower-bound simulation dependency through
  Lemma HS.1 in science/haar_simulation.md and its versioned primary source.
  Introductory explanations and understanding targets do not replace proofs.
- To allocate queries: read science/resource_tradeoffs.md together with U1,
  U2 and L1 in science/model.md. Check the integer budgets and dimension
  condition for the regime being discussed, then choose an implementation.
- To understand forward access alone: read science/forward_only.md and its
  QURA attribution. Distinguish native inverse calls from inverses synthesized
  by ordinary forward queries, all of which are charged.
- To reproduce a finite ingredient: read verification/README.md, install
  the documented requirements and run python3 verification/run_all.py from
  the repository root. Distinguish a fresh execution from an earlier report.

## Scientific distinctions to preserve

- The promise is W|0> = |0> or sqrt(1-epsilon^2)|0> + epsilon|1>, with both
  vectors and epsilon known. It is a one-bit decision problem, with no
  oracle-dependent advice or QRAM. It is narrower than general amplitude
  estimation for an unknown output state or arbitrary target subspace.
- One fixed W is reused throughout an experiment. The upper algorithm works
  separately for every completion under either hypothesis; it does not
  assume a common completion across hypotheses. The lower proof may choose
  a correlated pair W0 = 1 direct-sum U and W1 = R W0 as a hard ensemble.
- F and K are hard total caps along every classical measurement history,
  not expected costs, circuit depth or separately discounted counterfactual
  branches. Parallel calls count all oracle ports. The lower bound allows
  coherent skipping of the classically selected direction at full call cost.
  The upper algorithms use ordinary uncontrolled oracle calls.
- Lemma HS.1 proves a stronger switched-query simulation interface. That
  mathematical lemma does not extend the separate F,K lower-bound accounting
  to a coherent direction switch with fractional or counterfactual costs.
- U1 uses at most K calibration inverses, with no retry loop. A calibration
  outcome either certifies the alternative or gives one exact unknown state
  orthogonal to |0>. Coherent fixed-occupation loading uses the supplied copies.
  It does not assume a classical description or extra copies of that state.
- A collective variance alone is not the finite decision theorem. U1 also
  controls the fourth moment and rounded budgets and attains alternative
  success at least 735/1024 with zero null false positives in the exact model.
  Its fixed-occupation parallel optimality is a restricted statement.
- L1 covers arbitrary known processing and workspace with classically adaptive
  query directions. It uses d-1 a power of two and an explicit sufficient
  dimension condition depending on T = F+K. The two dimension errors remain
  part of the finite theorem. Logarithmic register width does not establish
  an efficient implementation of a Haar-random physical oracle.
- Projected histories in the proof remain subnormalized. The record potential
  tracks a sum of selected forward-output probabilities, bounded by K.
  Inverse rotations are removed at ordinal inverse-event boundaries; a bound
  on a sum of probabilities cannot be substituted for a sum of amplitudes.
- F(K+1)+K^2 asymptotic to epsilon^-2 describes the boundary up to universal
  factors in the stated large-dimension regime. It is not an equality imposed
  on every feasible budget pair. The rounded U1 and U2 budgets take precedence
  when a finite allocation or an endpoint constant matters.
- The weighted optimum Theta(min(sqrt(r)/epsilon, epsilon^-2)) for r >= 1
  is an oracle-cost conclusion under the same lower-bound dimension condition.
  The wide circuit and streaming circuit have different gate/memory pairs;
  their best separate costs are not a single established implementation.
- The all-dimension forward-only result is fewer than
  5 min(epsilon^-2, d/epsilon) ordinary forward calls, with no native inverse
  calls. It synthesizes only calibration inverses. This is an upper bound;
  the optimal fixed-dimension converse is not established here.
- The inverse-only measurement-discrimination endpoint, hidden-basis loading
  and QURA inversion are established constructions. Ma–Huang supplies the
  strong recording framework; the needed control/history extension and
  task-specific potential are derived here. Consult attribution before
  identifying the contribution or transferring a theorem between models.
- Childs is the sole educational anchor. Primary research sources retain
  their role in attribution and imported proof ingredients. Chapter 26's
  compressed classical-function oracle is a conceptual starting point;
  it is not the mixed Haar-unitary simulation theorem used in L1.
- The finite checks verify their enumerated constructive identities and
  budgets. Use the written arguments for the adaptive and asymptotic
  conclusions; numerical agreement does not establish external peer review.
